summary: All 11 TDD-anchor methods are present with strong behavioral assertions. Every edge case listed in Details is covered (unclosed brace, value-with-braces not re-parsed, parseMode=null→None, null/empty, null custom-fields map, null template). Both halves of the escaping contract are verified: htmlModeEscapesSubstitutedValues asserts author markup is preserved AND substituted values are HTML-escaped; markdownV2ModeEscapesFullCharset exercises all 19 official MarkdownV2 special chars in one payload. Negative injection cases are present in both escaping tests. Litmus test passed for all 19 test methods. Two minor findings logged but neither blocks the verdict.

findings.issue: The emptyOrNullValueRendersEmpty test covers {user.first_name} and {user.username} with null/empty values, but never exercises {user.last_name} with a null value through the template. The subscriber helper is called with last_name=null but {user.last_name} is absent from the rendered template string, so the last_name null-resolution path in userField() is not directly exercised.
findings.recommendation: Add '{user.last_name}' to the template in emptyOrNullValueRendersEmpty: render('[{user.first_name}][{user.last_name}][{user.username}][{custom.empty}][{custom.nil}]', null, s) and assert '[][][][][]'. This explicitly pins the last_name null→empty path.

findings.issue: The spec says 'Boolean → людський рядок (очікуваний рядок)' without specifying exact text. The test asserts 'true/false' which is JVM's default Boolean.toString(). This is correct behavior but the spec intent is underspecified — a future implementer changing to 'Yes'/'No' or 'Так'/'Ні' would break this test with no spec guidance. The assertion is not wrong, but the test comment should document why lowercase true/false was chosen.
findings.recommendation: Add a comment to rendersBooleanHumanReadable explaining the chosen representation: '// Boolean.toString() → lowercase true/false, consistent with Java conventions and Telegram plain text'. No assertion change needed.
